newsitem.title: USA: Rocket blasts off with communication satellite.
newsitem.headline: Rocket blasts off with communication satellite.

text.p: An international communications satellite designed to relay calls from a mobile telephone the size of a laptop computer rode atop an Atlas rocket that blasted into space on Tuesday.

The Lockheed Martin Corp Atlas 2 rocket gracefully climbed into the Florida night sky from its launch pad at Cape Canaveral Air Station at 8:57 p.m. EST (0157 GMT on Wednesday). The rocket's fiery climb to orbit was visible more than 140 miles (225 km) away.
Nestled in the slender rocket's nose cone was a new generation of powerful mobile communication satellites owned by the 79-nation Inmarsat consortium.
The $180 million mission was the third of five planned Inmarsat 3 satellite launches. The satellite was released into a temporary orbit about 32 minutes after blastoff.
The satellite was to later fire a rocket motor to round off its orbit. Its final location will be 22,300 miles (35,890 km) above the Pacific Ocean, two degrees east of the international dateline.

Calls can be placed via the constellation of satellites from almost anywhere on the planet using a $3,000 telephone terminal the size of a laptop computer. Telephone, fax and data calls on the system are charged at $3 per minute.
It was the 27th consecutive successful launch for the Atlas rocket, which started life in the 1950's as an intercontinental ballistic missile.
